classification.difficultyReason: Identify the axis point reached by a positive or negative quarter-turn multiple, then read its sine or cosine coordinate from the supplied unit circle.

content.prompt: Use the diagram below to find the exact value of the following.

spec.description: Unit circle with axis intercepts, a first-quadrant radius, coordinate projections and coordinate definitions. The origin letter is omitted under the house graph convention. Ordinary source marks are rendered black; no shading is used.
spec.mathematics: The radius is 1; P=(cos θ,sin θ). Dashed projections meet the coordinate axes.

answer.worked: At $0^{\circ}$ the unit-circle point is $(1,0)$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin(0^{\circ})=0$.
At $0^{\circ}$ the unit-circle point is $(1,0)$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos(0^{\circ})=1$.
At $90^{\circ}$ the unit-circle point is $(0,1)$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin(90^{\circ})=1$.
At $90^{\circ}$ the unit-circle point is $(0,1)$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos(90^{\circ})=0$.
A clockwise turn of $90^{\circ}$ reaches $(0,-1)$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin(-90^{\circ})=-1$.
A clockwise turn of $90^{\circ}$ reaches $(0,-1)$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos(-90^{\circ})=0$.
At $180^{\circ}$ the unit-circle point is $(-1,0)$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin(180^{\circ})=0$.
At $180^{\circ}$ the unit-circle point is $(-1,0)$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos(180^{\circ})=-1$.
A clockwise half-turn reaches $(-1,0)$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin(-180^{\circ})=0$.
A clockwise half-turn reaches $(-1,0)$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos(-180^{\circ})=-1$.
At $270^{\circ}$ the unit-circle point is $(0,-1)$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin(270^{\circ})=-1$.
At $270^{\circ}$ the unit-circle point is $(0,-1)$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos(270^{\circ})=0$.
A clockwise turn of $270^{\circ}$ reaches $(0,1)$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin(-270^{\circ})=1$.
A clockwise turn of $270^{\circ}$ reaches $(0,1)$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos(-270^{\circ})=0$.
A full turn returns to $(1,0)$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin(360^{\circ})=0$.
A full turn returns to $(1,0)$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos(360^{\circ})=1$.
